_doc: Per-page metadata for the Category-25 (Cannabis, Hemp, and CBD Products) standard renderer (tools/build-category-standard-pages.mjs). Numbers come from data/standards/cat25-compiled/<record>.json (frozen derivations from the index repo's deterministic compiler, tools/standards/compile-cat25.mjs); nothing numeric is authored here. Six rows are published: the five route rows plus the vape cartridge-fill (the consumable vape oil). Only the vape hardware / aerosol-emissions facet of taxonomy row 6 remains reserved (metal release into aerosol is a different measured quantity) and is intentionally NOT listed here.

_meta.methodology_version: Method v2.0 — government-limit default (route-split sovereign cannabis action levels; CLAUDE.md Part 19)
method_prose: Cannabis has no uniform federal contaminant limit. Its heavy-metal ceilings are the route-split action levels of the credible sovereign cannabis programs — California (DCC 2026), Colorado (2022), Massachusetts (2020), Maryland (2025), Nevada (2020), and Israel (IMC-GMP 152, 2016). For each analyte the HMTc limit is the strictest maximum any of these governments sets for the product's administration route. The route basis is never conflated: the strict inhaled arsenic and cadmium action levels are never applied to an edible or a topical, and a permissive topical lead level is never applied to inhaled flower. It is a lookup, not a computation; occurrence never selects a value.

Four analytes bind directly to a sovereign action level — lead, cadmium, total arsenic, and total mercury. Total chromium is recorded as a screening ceiling rather than a health limit: it is dominated by benign trivalent chromium while the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, so the total-chromium action level is non-protective as a ceiling and any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails certification. Nickel, tin, and aluminium, which no cannabis program regulates for content, are held under mandatory analytical control; inorganic arsenic, methylmercury, and hexavalent chromium are enforced by reflex speciation against their measured total. Certification is heavy-metal safety only and does not endorse the efficacy or the legality of these products.

pages.name: Cannabis flower and dried herb
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified heavy-metal-safety standard for cannabis flower and dried herb (Cannabis, Hemp, and CBD Products), evaluated on the finished inhalable product as sold. Each limit is the strictest sovereign cannabis heavy-metal action level applicable to the inhalation route; total chromium is a screening ceiling with hexavalent chromium as the binding control, and inorganic arsenic, methylmercury and Cr(VI) are enforced by reflex speciation.

pages.name: Cannabis vape cartridge fill (vape oil)
pages.description: The Heavy Metal Tested & Certified heavy-metal-safety standard for cannabis vape cartridge fill — the consumable vape oil, sometimes called 'juice' — evaluated on the finished inhalable consumable as sold. Each limit is the strictest sovereign cannabis heavy-metal action level applicable to the inhalation route (the same pool as flower); total chromium is a screening ceiling with hexavalent chromium as the binding control, and inorganic arsenic, methylmercury and Cr(VI) are enforced by reflex speciation. This standard covers the cartridge fill only; the vape hardware and its aerosol emissions are a separate reserved determination.
